chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about the one who died during the period (of the prophets), and about the one who did not incur sin, and the insane. So he (peace be upon him) said: Allah will present His argument against them. He will raise a fire for them and say to them: Enter it. So whoever enters it, it will be for him a coolness and peace, and whoever refuses, He will say: Behold, you are here. I commanded you, but you disobeyed Me.

key_terms.الْحِنْث: Sin or fault incurred by committing a religious duty or prohibition
key_terms.الْفَتْرَة: The period between two prophets, specifically the interval where no prophet was present
key_terms.بَرْداً وَ سَلَاماً: Coolness and peace/safety, indicating ease rather than punishment
key_terms.يَحْتَجُّ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ: Allah presents His argument/evidence against them

ai.seo_question: What happens to people who died between prophets or were insane according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the doctrine of divine justice (adl) for those excluded from the general call to prophethood, specifically detailing the fate of the insane (al-ma'tuh) and those who died in the interval between prophets (al-fatra). It establishes that Allah raises a barrier of fire as a test of submission; entry signifies acceptance of His command, while refusal confirms their status as disobedient, ensuring no soul is unjustly punished for lacking knowledge or capacity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the one who died during the era (between one Prophet<sup>as</sup> and the next), and about the one who did not perform violations (sins) and the insane. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Argue against them. He<sup>azwj</sup> would Raise a fire and He<sup>azwj</sup> would be Saying to them: “Enter!” So the one who enters it, it would be a coolness upon him and a safety, and to the one refuses, He<sup>azwj</sup> would Say: “Behold you all! I<sup>saww</sup> had Commanded you, but you disobeyed Me<sup>azwj</sup>!”’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hisham who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah was asked

about those who die in the interval (between the passing away of one prophet and coming of the other), those who have not committed sins, and people with severe mental conditions. He replied, ‘Allah argues against them by lighting up a fire and telling them to walk in it. Those who go in the fire it becomes cool and peaceful for them and to those who refuse Allah will say, “Consider, I just commanded you but you disobeyed Me.’””
